extracted.intended_audience: third parties and patent practitioners preparing preissuance submissions under 35 U.S.C. 122(e) / 37 CFR 1.290
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing third-party preissuance submissions under 35 U.S.C. 122(e) and 37 CFR 1.290, including required content, formatting, fees, evidence of publication, and compliance review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of foreign patents/published foreign patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(e)(3) permits identification of foreign patents and published foreign patent applications by expanding the identification to also include the applicant or patentee, in addition to the first named inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use flexibility permitted by rule to include applicant/patentee information when identifying foreign patent documents; ensure bibliographic data is not in error (e.g., transposed numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patent publication listing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(e)(4) requires that each non-patent publication be identified by author (if any), title, pages being submitted, publication date, and, where available, publisher and place of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publisher/place information is unavailable, provide what is available. For internet-obtained publications provide the URL of the web page that is the source, and where applicable both the archived page URL and the site URL (example given with Internet Archive Wayback Machine).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of publication when no date is known
rubrics_metrics.description: If no publication date is known for a non-patent document, 37 CFR 1.290(e)(4) requires the third party to provide evidence of publication and at least a date of retrieval or a time frame when the document was available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide retrieval date (e.g., date a webpage was retrieved) or a time frame (year, month and year, period) plus evidence establishing the document as a publication. See section III.A for more on acceptable evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise description of asserted relevance required
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(d)(2) requires a concise description of the asserted relevance of each item identified in the document list; this is a statement of facts regarding the submitted evidence and not itself evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The concise description should set forth facts explaining how the item is of potential relevance to examination. It may be narrative or a claim chart and is most effective when it draws the examiner’s attention to specific relevant pages, lines, figures, or paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise description must be more than bare statements
rubrics_metrics.description: At a minimum, a concise description of relevance must be more than a bare statement that the document is relevant (e.g., 'Document 1 is relevant' is insufficient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotated/highlighted copies alone are not proper concise descriptions. Avoid mere form paragraphs or general opposition statements. Focused descriptions (intro plus claim chart mapping portions to claim elements) are appropriate; verbose narratives that merely repeat claim charts or approach the length of the documents are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise descriptions must not insert unpublished material
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party submissions that include unpublished materials as attachments to or inserted into the text of a concise description of relevance will be found non-compliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relying on material not in the listed publication (e.g., an image from a different source), that other source must itself be published and separately listed for consideration; do not insert unpublished facts into the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise description is not an invitation to participate in prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: The concise description of relevance is limited to a factual description of a document’s relevance and must not propose rejections, argue against patentability, or set forth conclusions about claim patentability (unlike a protest under 37 CFR 1.291).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include arguments that rise to the level of a protest (e.g., 'It would have been obvious...' or 'The composition is unpatentable in view of...'); keep to factual mappings and explanations only. Examples of compliant vs. non-compliant narratives and claim charts are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted formats for concise description
rubrics_metrics.description: The concise description can be presented in any format that best explains relevance (e.g., narrative or claim chart).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise description that prominently identifies which item(s) it pertains to will assist screeners and examiners. When filing electronically, the web interface provides a concise description field or allows uploading a separate paper; in paper filings, provide as a separate paper; all descriptions may be combined in a single paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies requirement for submitted items
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(d)(3) requires submission of a legible copy of each item identified in the document list, other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications (which need not be submitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color copies will be scanned to black and white. No CDs or other physical electronic media for paper filings; electronic uploads are permitted via the Office’s web interface. If only a portion of a document is listed, submit a copy of that portion and pages that provide identifying information (cover, title page, copyright page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling of items and corresponding materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practice: include an identifying label for each item in the document list and place that label on the concise description, the copy of the item (if submitted), and the translation (if submitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels help screeners and examiners quickly identify which descriptions, copies, and translations correspond to each listed item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of NPL images and file handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Images of non-patent literature cited in a compliant third-party submission will not be available for viewing/downloading through Patent Center; the Office separates the document list from copies so bibliographic information is visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office practice mirrors IDS handling under 37 CFR 1.98; be aware images may not be retrievable from Patent Center even if entered into the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for non-English items
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(d)(4) requires an English language translation of any non-English language item identified in the document list; the translation may be a reliable machine translation and need not be certified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only a portion of a non-English document is listed, submit a copy of the listed portion and a translation of only that portion (do not submit translation of entire document when only a portion is listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements required from submitter
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(d)(5)(i) requires a statement that the party making the submission is not an individual who has a duty to disclose under 37 CFR 1.56; 37 CFR 1.290(d)(5)(ii) requires a statement that the submission complies with 35 U.S.C. 122(e) and 37 CFR 1.290; the 1.290(g) statement is required to claim the fee exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/429 and the web interface include the required statements. Submissions must be signed (37 CFR 1.4). Office will not entertain challenges to the accuracy of such statements; false statements are subject to penalties under 18 U.S.C. 1001.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and identity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A third-party submission must be signed by the submitter; the Office cannot permit submissions presented unsigned. There is no requirement to identify a real party in interest; a real party can remain anonymous by having someone else submit on their behalf, but the submitter cannot remain anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature requirement enforces accountability; required statements (d)(5) and (g) must be signed by the person making the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee: general rule and item counting
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(f) requires payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(o) for every ten items or fraction thereof listed in the document list, except where the submission is accompanied by the 1.290(g) statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office counts items based on the 1.290(d)(1) document list. U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications identified in the list are counted even if copies are not submitted. Portions listed count as one item. Multiple publications from the same website are counted as separate items. If a copy is submitted but the item is not identified in the list it will be discarded and not counted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee exemption (37 CFR 1.290(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee exemption is available where a third-party submission lists three or fewer total items and is the first third-party submission by that third party (or a party in privity) in a given application, provided the submission is accompanied by the 1.290(g) statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 1.290(g) statement must assert, to the knowledge of the signer after reasonable inquiry, that the submission is the 'first and only' third-party submission by that third party or a party in privity. Other third parties not in privity may also take the exemption. Third parties may instead choose to pay the fee even for a three-or-fewer item first submission if unsure about asserting privity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity discount and micro entity ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A small entity discount is available for third-party submission fees where applicable; a micro entity discount is not available for third-party submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To claim small entity when filing in paper, select the 'small entity' box on form PTO/SB/429 (or select 'Small Entity' in the electronic filing system) and pay the applicable small entity fee. Selecting the box asserts small entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission after finding of non-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a third party receives a notification of non-compliance, the third party may revise and resubmit a complete corrected submission within the statutory filing period; resubmissions must be complete submissions (no amendments) and must be accompanied by the appropriate fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the non-compliant submission included the proper fee, the Office may apply that previously-paid fee to the resubmission at its discretion. The Office will not accept mere amendments to non-compliant submissions; the resubmission must be another complete submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed publications limitation and acceptable content
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 122(e)(1) and 37 CFR 1.290(a) limit third-party submissions to patents, published patent applications, and other printed publications of potential relevance (e.g., published articles, Office actions in published applications, communications from foreign patent offices in published foreign applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials that do not qualify as publications (e.g., items subject to protective orders or secrecy, trade secrets, unpublished internal documents intended to be confidential, emails not widely disseminated) must not be submitted; physical samples must not be submitted and will be discarded. Published information that is visual output (software screenshots, video) must be reduced to writing (e.g., screenshots) and evidence of publication provided if date not known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance review and consequences of non-publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions under 37 CFR 1.290 will be reviewed for compliance before being forwarded to an examiner. If any submitted document is found not to be a publication on its face, the entire submission will be found non-compliant and discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission is determined compliant, publications will be considered by the examiner and entered into the file as required by 35 U.S.C. 122(e). An applicant may challenge the Office’s determination that a document is a publication in response to a rejection applying the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of publication: form and content
rubrics_metrics.description: When items are not prima facie publications, a third party must submit evidence establishing they are publications. Evidence may be affidavits, declarations, or other appropriate formats and must be specific to the documents submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits/declarations must comply with Office formal requirements (notary/acknowledgment; declarations must include 18 U.S.C. 1001 admonition and statements of personal knowledge where appropriate). Evidence must be limited to facts establishing why the document qualifies as a publication and not used to place irrelevant information before the examiner. Examples: employee declaration that brochures were distributed at a trade show, email showing public dissemination, website printouts or screenshots showing content available on a particular date, archived web page URLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of publication does not count toward item count unless itself a publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence submitted to establish publication (e.g., affidavits, screenshots) will not be counted toward the document item count for fee purposes unless the evidence itself is a patent document or other printed publication and is listed and submitted for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies provided to satisfy copy requirements may serve as evidence (e.g., a website printout showing retrieval date) but will only be counted as items if they are themselves listed as publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement that submitted information be prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(a) does not require that submitted information be prior art; third parties do not need to indicate whether a listed document is asserted to be prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For documents where publication date is not apparent, provide date information in the concise description of relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative information permitted but discouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(a) does not prohibit submissions that include documents already of record or cumulative of each other, though best practice is to avoid purely cumulative submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because submissions may include both publications and descriptions of their relevance, identifying purely cumulative submissions is difficult. Use discretion to avoid unnecessary duplication but submissions that are otherwise compliant may still be entered.
